THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:

JUDGMENT Heard the learned counsel for appellant and learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent/State and perused the material on record.
2.
Respondent No.2 is served but there is no representation.

3. Halasur Police registered a case in Crime No.184/2016 on 26.05.2016 against the appellant and four others for offence punishable under Section 3(1)(x) of the SC/ST (POA) Act, 1989 and Sections 506, 143, 323 r/w 149 of IPC, on a complaint lodged by one Rajalakshmi- respondent No.2.
4.

The gist of the complaint is that earlier there was a case registered in Crime No.156/2016 for offences punishable under Sections 506, 376, 504, 420 r/w 34 of IPC against the appellant and others and in this background on 25.05.2016 at about 7.30-8.00 p.m. when the complainant was returning from her work place, the appellant/accused No.1 and his family members assaulted her with hands, threatened her and abused her insulting her caste etc.
5.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for appellant that in so far as Crime No.156/2016 is concerned, the trial is at fag end.
He submits that the appellant herein was not at all present in India when the alleged incident took place.
On the other hand, he was abroad and therefore contends that the entire allegations are false and the appellant being innocent has been falsely implicated in this case.
He would also submit that the trial held against accused Nos.2 to 4 has ended in acquittal and in the said case the complainant and other material witnesses have not supported the prosecution case.
6. The learned counsel for appellant has annexed a copy of the judgment dated 01.12.2022 passed in Spl.C.No.1060/2019.

A perusal of the same goes to show that accused Nos.2 to 4 were acquitted of Adeebulla Sharief vs State By Halasuru Police on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90320627/
2 the charges leveled against them under Sections 143, 323, 506 r/w 149 of IPC and Sections 3 (1)(r)(s) and 3(2)(va) of SC/ST (POA) Act 1989.
7.

sentences.text: The appellant herein preferred Criminal Misc No.112/2023 under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. which has been rejected by the learned Sessions Judge by an order dated 02.02.2023.

It is observed therein that a caste based attack has been made on the complainant in public view and in view of prima facie materials attracting Section 3 of the SC/ST Act, the Court has no jurisdiction to entertain the petition seeking grant of anticipatory bail.
8. Learned High Court Government Pleader has contended that the appellant was absconding and therefore a separate split up case was registered against him in Spl.C.No.1254/2021.
Further, the proclamation warrant issued by the trial Court under Section 83 of Cr.P.C. was also duly published and this appellant has been declared as proclaimed offender.
He therefore contends that the appellant is not entitled for anticipatory bail as rightly held by the learned Special Court.
9. A perusal of the complaint averments does not disclose that this appellant has made any caste based attack on the complainant.
It is alleged that all the accused assaulted the complainant with hands and appellant's mother and aunt threatened her and also abused her referring to her caste.

Hence, on reading of the complaint it cannot be said that there is a prima facie case against the appellant to attract the provisions of the SC/ST Act so as to deny him the benefit of anticipatory bail.
Secondly, the learned counsel for appellant has produced a copy of the passport with relevant pages to show that the appellant was not in the country at the time of alleged incident.
It is however a matter for trial.
10. It is not in dispute that accused Nos.2 to 4 who faced trial have been acquitted by the learned Sessions Judge.
A perusal of the deposition of PW.1 i.e., the complainant shows that she has not supported the case of prosecution.
In the above facts and circumstances, the relief sought by the appellant can be granted by imposing conditions.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER Appeal is allowed.
The order dated 02.02.2023 passed by the Court of LXX Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge and Special Judge, Bengaluru in Criminal Misc No.112/2023, is set aside.
